headline: 1,314 hospitalised in 24 hours: 4 die of dengue in record surge
summary: A single-day record for hospitalisations was hit as the DGHS reports a sharp rise in cases, prompting DSCC to order urgent mosquito control operations.
details: Four people died of dengue in the last 24 hours, while 1,314 were admitted to hospitals. According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), this marks the highest number of single-day hospitalisations recorded this year.
As of September 6, a total of 42,590 people have been hospitalised and 117 have died from dengue across the country this year.
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Md. Abdus Salam has ordered an intensified and coordinated mosquito control campaign to combat the worsening situation.
A recent DSCC survey revealed a worrying trend, with mosquito larvae found in approximately 60% of the households surveyed.

caption:
A record-breaking surge in dengue cases: 1,314 people hospitalised in just 24 hours.

Four people died of dengue in the last 24 hours, while 1,314 were admitted to hospitals. According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), this marks the highest number of single-day hospitalisations recorded this year.

As of September 6, a total of 42,590 people have been hospitalised and 117 have died from dengue across the country this year.

Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Md. Abdus Salam has ordered an intensified and coordinated mosquito control campaign to combat the worsening situation.

A recent DSCC survey revealed a worrying trend, with mosquito larvae found in approximately 60% of the households surveyed.

Administrator Salam emphasized that insecticides alone are not enough. He stressed the need to destroy mosquito breeding sites, conduct regular cleaning drives, and involve citizens directly in the process.

Citizens are urged to remove stagnant water from courtyards, rooftops, flower pots, and abandoned containers after rain to prevent mosquitoes from breeding.
